evidence_summary: Effects Database identifies the Applied FW-3 as a U.S.-made multi-effect combining fuzz, wah, and volume. The same source enumerates a cluster of OEM-marketed versions under Guild, Crown, Kadent, Jax-USA, Atlantic, Lou Rose, Magnum, Nomad, and V-Jay.
The Nomad Fuzz Wah is separately cataloged as an Applied FW-3 family product. This is distinct from the unresolved early Nomad Super Fuzz and from the Nomad Tone Booster linked to UMI.
Effects Database identifies the Magnum FW-3 as an Applied Audio product and places it in the same OEM FW-3 family.
Atlantic FW-3 is cataloged as an Applied Audio product in the same OEM family. Its relationship is model-specific and does not imply Atlantic controlled the factory.
Jax-USA FW-3 is cataloged as manufactured by Applied Audio and sold under the Jax-USA name as part of the OEM line.
Lou Rose FW-3 is cataloged as an Applied Audio product distributed through Lou Rose Music in Edison, New Jersey. The model belongs to the same FW-3 OEM family.
Crown FW-3 is cataloged as a U.S.-made Applied Audio product and shares the FW-3 family identity with the other branded versions.
Kadent FW-3 is cataloged as produced by Applied Audio and sold under the Kadent name. The family relationship is model-specific rather than inferred from cosmetic similarity.

Effects Database catalogs the V-Jay FW-3 as Applied-made, but portions of the current entry contain detailed construction and dating claims that should be treated cautiously until corroborated by period documentation. The family assignment itself is retained as research-grade.

physical_builder_candidate: LIMMCO as house-brand/distribution context; Applied Audio as physical builder
evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies Nomad as a LIMMCO house brand and separately identifies Nomad Fuzz Wah as an Applied FW-3 state. This supports a LIMMCO-to-Applied supply-chain connection for this specific model state, not a blanket rule for all Nomad products.

The early Nomad Super Fuzz must remain isolated from the later Applied FW-3 Nomad Fuzz Wah. Current research describes a germanium Fuzzrite-type relationship but does not establish an Applied Audio build or a direct Mosrite OEM transaction.
